Layout step with one section per view

Source: R/pipeline.R
pub_layout_sections.Rd

Makes the function of a layout step (see pub_doc()) whose document has one section per view: the section is titled by the name of the view and shows the outputs of the steps of the view, in pipeline order. Select the steps of each section with pipeflow::pip_view(), e.g. by a tag naming the section or by the steps that depend on a model fit. Add the layout step with pipeflow::pip_add() (see Examples).

Usage

pub_layout_sections(sections)

Arguments

sections

Named list of pipeflow views of one pipeline, one per section, named by the section titles. The views must not contain other layout steps (a document can't be part of a document).

Value

A function for pipeflow::pip_add(). It takes the outputs of the steps of the views (~try(step)) and returns a pub_doc().

Details

This is a ready-made layout on top of pub_layout_inputs(), which gives the inputs for a layout function you write yourself (e.g. one section per step). The inputs behave as there: running the layout step runs only the steps it needs, a failed input is shown as an error box in its section, the steps are read when pub_layout_sections() is called (so add the layout step last), and partitioned outputs together with other outputs need exec = "reduce".

A step in several views appears in each of their sections (not a table or figure with an id, which must be unique in a document). A section whose outputs are all NULL is left out (see on_empty of pub_section()), so a step can leave its section out by returning NULL, e.g. if a param switches it off.

See also

pub_layout_inputs() for other layouts.

Examples

p <- pipeflow::pip_new("ozone") |>
    pipeflow::pip_add("data", \(month = 5) {
        subset(airquality, Month == month, select = c(Day, Ozone, Temp))
    }) |>
    pipeflow::pip_add("table", \(data = ~data) {
        pub_table(head(data), caption = "First days")
    }, tags = "Data") |>
    pipeflow::pip_add("fit", \(data = ~data) {
        stats::lm(Ozone ~ Temp, data = data)
    }) |>
    pipeflow::pip_add("slope", \(fit = ~fit, show_model = param(TRUE)) {
        if (!show_model) {
            return(NULL)
        }
        pub_format_num(stats::coef(fit)[["Temp"]], "Slope: %.2f ppb per degree F")
    })

layout <- pub_layout_sections(list(
    Data = pipeflow::pip_view(p, tags = "Data"),
    Model = pipeflow::pip_view(p, depends = "fit")
))
pipeflow::pip_add(p, "doc", layout)
pipeflow::pip_run(p, lgr = NULL)
p[["doc", "out"]]
#> <pubflow document>
#> # Data
#>   table "First days"
#> # Model
#>   text "Slope: 1.88 ppb per degree F"

# The model section is left out if its only step returns NULL
pipeflow::pip_set_params(p, list(show_model = FALSE))
pipeflow::pip_run(p, lgr = NULL)
p[["doc", "out"]]
#> <pubflow document>
#> # Data
#>   table "First days"
